# `starhermit:canvas`

Engine **1.40.0** (host API 1.40), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:canvas";
```

Offscreen 2D canvases in the HTML Canvas 2D model, rasterized by the engine (`starhermit-canvas`), usable as scene textures and overlay images. Supported members keep the web's names and semantics; invalid string settings (colors, fonts, enum values) are ignored as on the web, and non-finite path or drawing arguments do nothing. Bounds: 4,096 pixels on a side and 8,388,608 pixels per canvas, 100,000 path segments and 524,288 points per draw, 4,096 characters per text call, 1,024 gradient stops, 256 dash entries, 1,024 nested saves, 32 MiB of clip masks, shadow blur at most 512, and about 0.2 s of drawing work per call (each text character counts); past one a call throws a RangeError ("drawing too complex" for the work). All canvases and image bitmaps of a game together hold at most 256 MiB (RangeError).

The work budget. Drawing is counted in work units, each about a nanosecond of the engine's rasterizer on a desktop core: one call does at most 200,000,000, and all of a game's canvases share 200,000,000 a frame (refilled as each frame begins, natively and in browsers alike). A call is charged its whole estimate before it changes a pixel:

- Shapes (`fill`, `stroke`, `fillRect`, `strokeRect`, `clearRect`, `drawImage`, text's glyphs): each pixel of the shape's bounding box within the canvas and the clip costs 2 for a solid color drawn `source-over` inside a rectangular clip, 12 for any other `globalCompositeOperation` or under a clip path; a gradient adds 6, an image or pattern drawn at any scale 10 (`drawImage` too) and rotated, skewed or repeated 24. Rasterizing adds 4 units for each edge of the outline in each pixel row it crosses (a little more where many edges cross one row). A shadow adds 40 a pixel of its blurred layer and 10 to 14 a pixel it covers. `clip()` costs 2 a pixel of the clip's box plus its edges.
- Text: `fillText`, `strokeText` and `measureText` cost 8,000 a character, then the glyphs draw as shapes; a colour emoji also costs 8 a pixel of its image at the device's scale, drawn as an image.
- Pixels: `getImageData`, `putImageData` and `createPattern` of a canvas or ImageData cost 4 a pixel.

A call the frame's budget cannot cover draws nothing and throws a RangeError, "canvas work budget spent"; the next frame has the whole budget again. The work also counts against the calling entry's fuel (an instruction for each 10 units). For scale: a solid fill of a whole 2048 × 2048 canvas is about 8.4 M units (about 23 a frame), a gradient over it 34 M, `drawImage` of a 2048 × 2048 image 50 M (4 a frame) and 1,000 characters of text at least 8 M. So draw what does not change once and reuse it (draw the baked canvas with `drawImage`, `draw.image` or a `CanvasTexture`) rather than drawing it again each frame; spread a large bake over several frames (a few tiles a frame, or catch that RangeError and go on with the rest next frame); keep canvases no larger than they show; and leave shadows off large shapes.

GPU images: a canvas takes one of the game's images (120 unless `engine.limits.images` raises it, up to 1,024 since API\_MINOR 21) and its pixels' bytes of the image budget only once the overlay draws it or a CanvasTexture shows it; drawn onto other canvases it costs neither (see `engine.Budgets`).

Large textures: a canvas is at most 8,388,608 pixels (4096 × 2048) and a game's images share 56 MiB of GPU memory unless its manifest raises the budget (`engine.limits.image_mib`, up to 512 MiB since API\_MINOR 9), mipmaps adding a third; a 4096 × 4096 image with mipmaps alone would take 85 MiB. Draw repeating detail (line markings, grass, tiles) once on a small canvas and repeat it (`texture.wrapS = wrapT = RepeatWrapping` with `texture.repeat`), or split a large surface into several meshes, each with its own canvas of at most 2048 pixels a side. Not supported: `filter`, `imageSmoothingQuality` above "low" (it is recorded only), `fontStretch`, `fontVariantCaps`, `textRendering`, `lab()`/`lch()`/`oklab()`/`oklch()`/`color()` colors, `currentcolor` (black), focus rings, `isContextLost`, blobs and transfers.

  At most 4,096 pixels on a side and 8,388,608 pixels in all (4096 × 2048, or 2896 × 2896), natively and in browsers alike (the engine draws canvases itself, not the browser): a RangeError past either, also when `width` or `height` is set; 0 is allowed (draws nothing).

### createImageBitmap

*function*

```ts
export function createImageBitmap(source: string | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer | ImageData | OffscreenCanvas): Promise<ImageBitmap>;
```

Decodes a package image or image bytes, PNG or WebP (an animated WebP's first frame; rejects with an Error named `EncodingError` for data it cannot decode, a RangeError past 4,096 pixels on a side). Images decode off the game's thread, two at a time, and settle as a frame begins; at most 128 wait at once, an image's bytes are at most 16 MiB and those waiting at most 64 MiB together (RangeError, before they are copied). A package image is read without waiting for it (see `PackageFiles`). ImageData and canvases are copied at once.

### FontFace

*class*

A font from the package (TTF, OTF, TTC or OTC), as the web's FontFace.

```ts
export class FontFace { … }
```

- `constructor(family: string, source: string | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer, descriptors?: { style?: string; weight?: string; stretch?: string });`
- `readonly family: string;`
- `readonly status: "unloaded" | "loading" | "loaded" | "error";`

- `load(): Promise<FontFace>;`

  Reads the file without waiting for it (in browsers fetched first when the page has not; see `PackageFiles`). Rejects with an Error named `NetworkError` for a missing file and `SyntaxError` for data it cannot read.

### FontFaceSet

*interface*

The fonts canvases (and `draw.text`) can use, as `document.fonts`. At most 64 faces and 64 MiB of font data (RangeError); a face deleted and added again counts once.

```ts
export interface FontFaceSet { … }
```

- `add(font: FontFace): this;`
- `delete(font: FontFace): boolean;`
- `has(font: FontFace): boolean;`
- `readonly size: number;`

- `load(font: string, text?: string): Promise<FontFace[]>;`

  Loads what `text` (default `" "`) drawn in `font` (a CSS font value, as `context.font`) needs, as the web's `document.fonts.load`, and resolves with the set's faces of the families `font` names. Faces the game added are read as they are added, so what it waits for is the engine's emoji font, which loads only when text first needs it: when `text` has emoji (or symbols only that font has), this asks for it and resolves once it is in (or could not be loaded). A canvas draws once, so bake emoji only after this: drawn before the font arrives they stay blank (`fillText` asks for the font too, but does not wait). Rejects with a SyntaxError for a value `context.font` ignores. Since engine 1.20.1 (any minor).

- `check(font: string, text?: string): boolean;`

  Whether `text` in `font` draws now, as `document.fonts.check`: false while the emoji font it needs is on its way (asking starts loading it, where browsers' `check` loads nothing). SyntaxError for an invalid value. Since engine 1.20.1 (any minor).

- `readonly status: "loading" | "loaded";`

  `"loading"` while the emoji font is on its way, else `"loaded"`. Since engine 1.20.1 (any minor).

- `readonly ready: Promise<FontFaceSet>;`

  Settles once no font is on its way: once text asked for the emoji font, when it is in (or failed); at once otherwise (before engine 1.20.1 always at once).
